extracted.intended_audience: Researchers/applicants applying for NIH grants (R01, K, F, R21, R03, SBIR, etc.) who want practical timelines, status-expectations, and procedural tips
extracted.subtask_description: Collection of community timelines and practical guidance about NIH peer review and award-processing milestones (eRA Commons statuses, JIT, council, NOA), plus tips about interacting with Program Officers, Grants Management, and handling administrative requirements for funding.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scientific Review Group (SRG) review status
rubrics_metrics.description: Commons messages such as “Scientific Review Group review pending” and “Scientific Review Group review completed: Council review pending. Refer any questions to Program Official.” indicate SRG review stage and whether the application was discussed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: SRG review yields impact scores/summary statements; if listed as 'not discussed' the application may receive no score. Refer questions to the Scientific Review Administrator. Dates of SRG review are common timeline anchors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Impact score and percentile as evaluation metrics
rubrics_metrics.description: Impact score and percentile (when provided) are the main numeric outputs of peer review — e.g., “Impact score:20”, “21st percentile”, “no percentile given” for some mechanisms.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Lower impact score / lower percentile is better and strongly influences funding likelihood, but paylines vary by IC and fiscal availability. Some mechanisms (Ks) may have no percentile. Use score + PO guidance + payline history to estimate chances.

rubrics_metrics.name: Summary Statement availability and content
rubrics_metrics.description: Summary statements are released after SRG review and provide reviewer critiques; posts reference “Summary Statement available” and summary statements prompting PO contact or rebuttal requests.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Read summary carefully; Program Officers may request rebuttal/response letters or suggest resubmission. Summary statement often triggers outreach to PO and/or JIT activity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Council review milestone
rubrics_metrics.description: Status messages like “Council review completed” indicate the IC-level advisory council review has occurred (sometimes with a council meeting date).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Council actions and dates are important for final funding decisions; council may influence whether an application moves to administrative review. Note that council timing can delay processing toward award.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pending administrative review
rubrics_metrics.description: Commons status “Pending administrative review. Refer any questions to Program Official or Grants Management Specialist.” indicates IC-level and administrative checks prior to award preparation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Administrative review often precedes JIT or award preparation. Contact Program Official or GMS for administrative questions; status changes here are not guarantees of award.

rubrics_metrics.name: Just-in-Time (JIT) requests and materials
rubrics_metrics.description: “JIT requested”, “JIT submitted”, and multiple JIT requests appear frequently; JIT may ask for IRB/IACUC approvals, confirmation of degree conferral, revised budgets, earliest possible start date, and other documents.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Respond quickly and completely to JIT requests; editors note JITs can be repeated and missing approvals (IRB/IACUC) can delay award. Some JITs are 'non-automatic' (e.g., EOY funding) and require extra documentation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Award preparation and Notice of Award (NOA)
rubrics_metrics.description: Statuses “Award prepared: refer questions to Grants Management Specialist.” and “NOA received”/“Application awarded” mark final administrative steps and issuance of Notice of Award.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: After 'award prepared' there may still be short delays before NOA appears. NOA contains start date and budget adjustments; check it carefully for budget cuts and start date accuracy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Grants Management Specialist (GMS) role
rubrics_metrics.description: GMS is cited as contact during award preparation and for JIT/admin matters (“refer questions to Grants Management Specialist”).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Direct administrative and award-setup questions to the GMS. They handle JIT logistics and award paperwork; PO handles programmatic aspects.

rubrics_metrics.name: Program Officer (PO) engagement and communication
rubrics_metrics.description: Posts stress early/ongoing contact with the PO, reporting that PO feedback can indicate funding likelihood, request rebuttals, or advise resubmission. PO responsiveness varies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Engage POs early, ask about programmatic fit and budget, provide rebuttals or responses if requested, and use PO input to decide whether to resubmit. Do not assume silence means rejection; timelines vary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rebuttal/response to reviewers
rubrics_metrics.description: Examples mention PO requests for a short response to reviewers (e.g., '3-page response to reviewers', 'rebuttal letter submitted').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prepare concise, evidence-based responses addressing reviewer concerns when asked. Submit promptly and coordinate with PO if they request a specific format or length.

rubrics_metrics.name: Resubmission and persistence strategy
rubrics_metrics.description: Many posters describe multiple submissions (A0, A1, A2, etc.) with improving impact scores across resubmissions and advise persistence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Resubmissions can substantially improve scores; incorporate new data and reviewer feedback. Persistence and continued publication can increase fundability, but balance effort vs. diminishing returns.

rubrics_metrics.name: Institutional approvals and human/animal subject clearances
rubrics_metrics.description: IRB and IACUC approvals are commonly requested in JIT and can be required before award (examples: IRB approval delayed funding; JIT requesting IACUC).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Obtain and submit required approvals promptly; delays in approvals can block or postpone awards. Track timelines and coordinate with institutional offices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Budget rules, caps, and allowable costs
rubrics_metrics.description: Mentor/administrative salaries may be disallowed on some mechanisms (quoted: 'Salary for mentors, secretarial and administrative assistants, etc. is not allowed'); modular budgets, budget cuts, and salary caps (example: $75K vs $70K) are discussed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow FOA and IC-specific rules for allowable costs. You can often revise the budget at JIT; expect potential budget reductions. Consult GMS about what can/cannot be charged to the award.

rubrics_metrics.name: Early-Stage Investigator (ESI) and special payline considerations
rubrics_metrics.description: ESI status and programmatic priorities (e.g., ADRD, ESI payline changes) can affect funding likelihood; posters note ESI/ADRD percentiles and IC announcements influence expectations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If you are ESI, check IC-specific payline policies and announcements. Discuss ESI status with PO since it may increase probability of funding even at higher percentiles.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fiscal-year / EOY funding effects
rubrics_metrics.description: End-of-year (EOY) or fiscal-year timing can affect whether an application is funded that cycle (examples: 'considered for EOY funding', 'timing to keep it in fiscal year ending 8/31').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be aware that ICs may use end-of-year funds to pick up additional applications; timing can speed or delay awards. Track council dates relative to fiscal calendar.

rubrics_metrics.name: eRA Commons statuses are informative but not definitive
rubrics_metrics.description: Multiple posts warn that eRA status changes (e.g., 'Award Prepared' then back to 'Pending administrative review') are not guaranteed indicators of award.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use commons statuses as signals but confirm with PO/GMS. Status can change retroactively or fluctuate; do not interpret interim changes as final.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ability to revise budget at JIT
rubrics_metrics.description: Poster notes: 'you have the chance to revise your budget at the time of JIT request... they accepted the revised budget which was asking for a little more.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prepare a justified revised budget if needed; some ICs accept modest upward revisions at JIT, but approval is not guaranteed and is subject to IC/GMS review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Non-automatic JIT and special selection processes
rubrics_metrics.description: Occasionally applications receive 'non-automatic JIT' (e.g., 'considered for EOY funding') requiring additional steps or contingency handling.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If notified of non-automatic JIT, follow PO/GMS instructions precisely and provide requested documentation quickly; outcomes can be discretionary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Study section vs. Special Emphasis Panel (SEP) differences
rubrics_metrics.description: Some applications were reviewed by SEPs versus chartered study sections; status lines can indicate different review pathways (example: R34 reviewed by an SEP).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be aware that different review bodies may have different norms (scores, percentiles, discussion patterns). Confirm with PO how SEP review may affect outcomes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Administrative/technical document requests beyond JIT
rubrics_metrics.description: POs or GMS may request additional documentation (e.g., data records IDs, clarification of approvals, start date confirmation) after review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Respond promptly and accurately to ad-hoc requests from PO/GMS; missing documents can delay or jeopardize awards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Payline and budget availability dependence
rubrics_metrics.description: Funding decisions depend on payline and availability of funds (e.g., 'Pay line will depend on availability of funds and therefore an FY18 budget allocation from the Congress').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Understand that even good scores depend on IC budget; consult historical payline data and PO comments to form expectations, but be prepared for uncertainty.

rubrics_metrics.name: Start date and project period negotiation
rubrics_metrics.description: NOA contains project start date; posters note start dates sometimes differ from earlier expectations and may be adjusted (e.g., awarded with start date later than submission).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Verify the NOA start date and negotiate earliest feasible start if necessary; changes to start date can affect salary, hiring, and institutional planning.

rubrics_metrics.name: Using community timelines as heuristic but not authoritative
rubrics_metrics.description: The page is a collection of timelines from other awardees and includes the explicit caution that eRA status histories are not guaranteed indicators of awards.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use shared timelines to set expectations about timing and typical sequences, but rely on PO/GMS and official notices for authoritative determinations.
